title: One pure readiness derivation over a projected issue set
description:
Add one pure domain function that, given the issues before and after a mutation, returns the readiness corrections the dependency graph demands for the issues that mutation can affect. Every mutation that changes a state or a dependency will compute its dependent corrections through it.

## Background

- `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` (`crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs:714-723`) decides one issue: a `Backlog` issue nothing blocks is `Promote`, a `Ready` issue with an unmet dependency is `Demote` (`ReadinessCorrection`, `domain/types.rs:605`). `Issue::is_blocked` (`:673`) reads only `is_dependency_met` (`:151`) of each dependency, so a correction (which moves an issue only between the non-terminal `Backlog` and `Ready`) never changes another issue's blockedness: one pass over the projected set is complete.
- Every caller today chooses its own candidate set by hand: deletion walks the deleted issue's dependents (`derive_issue_deletion`, `crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:67-150`), dependency edits look at the edited source only (`crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs:605,964`), template edges look at the edge source (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:1281,1342`), `check_auto_transitions` (`commands/issue.rs:860-876`) scans every issue for promotions only, and `jit validate --fix` scans every issue in both directions.
- Nothing yet states which issues a mutation can affect, so there is no single place to prove that a correction is neither missed nor applied to unrelated drift.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A pure domain function takes the issues before a mutation, the issues after it and a scope, and returns each correction as an issue id with its `ReadinessCorrection`, ordered by issue id; it reads no storage and uses `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` for each candidate.
- [hard] REQ-02: The `Affected` scope admits exactly the issues that are new, whose dependency list changed, or that directly depend on an issue whose effective terminal state changed or which was removed; the `All` scope admits every projected issue.
- [hard] REQ-03: Unit tests cover promotion on a blocker reaching `Done` or `Rejected`, demotion on a blocker leaving a terminal state, demotion on an added edge, promotion on a removed edge or a deleted blocker, and no correction for `InProgress`, `Gated`, terminal or archived dependents.
- [hard] REQ-04: A property test over generated acyclic issue sets and single edits (state change, edge add or remove, deletion) shows that applying the `Affected` corrections leaves no issue whose stored readiness disagrees with the graph, and that no correction falls outside the `Affected` set.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged: no caller uses the function yet.
- Graph-rule gating of promotions stays in the command layer; this function only states what the graph demands.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: A pure domain function returns the Ready and Backlog corrections that a projected issue set implies.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One pure function with its unit and property tests, no caller migration.

title: Graph edits carry readiness corrections through one helper
description:
Give the command layer one helper that turns the pure readiness corrections into mutation intents, and make deletion, dependency edits and template edges use it, so the three graph-editing paths derive dependent readiness the same way inside their own plan.

## Background

- The pure derivation returns readiness corrections for a base and a projected issue set under an `Affected` or `All` scope.
- Deletion promotes dependents inside its plan through `derive_state_transition` (`derive_issue_deletion`, `crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:67-150`, promotion at `:103-140`).
- `jit dep rm` promotes the edited source through `derive_state_transition` (`derive_dependency_removal`, `crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs:515`, promotion at `:605-639`); `jit dep add` and the reduction demote directly (`derive_reduced_graph_intents`, `dependency.rs:922`, demotion at `:964-974`).
- Template application demotes directly on edge addition (`add_captured_template_edge`, `crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:1209`, `:1281-1291`) and promotes directly on edge removal, bypassing graph rules (`remove_captured_template_edge`, `template.rs:1305`, `:1342-1353`).
- `derive_state_transition` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:1073`) applies graph rules to a promotion and returns `GraphBlocked` with `transition_blocked` events when one refuses it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One helper beside `derive_state_transition` in `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs` maps the pure corrections over a base and a projected issue set to mutation intents: a promotion goes through `derive_state_transition` (graph rules apply; a refused promotion records its `transition_blocked` events and its error is reported after apply), a demotion is applied directly with its state-change event.
- [hard] REQ-02: Issue deletion, `dep add`, `dep rm`, dependency reduction and template edge addition and removal obtain their dependent readiness changes only from that helper; none of them calls `derive_readiness_correction` or `should_auto_transition_to_ready` directly.
- [hard] REQ-03: For each of the three command families (deletion, dependency edits, template application) one harness test shows the dependent's correction published in the same session as the primary change.
- [hard] REQ-04: A harness test shows that removing a template edge whose promotion a graph rule refuses leaves the dependent in `Backlog` and records `transition_blocked`; it fails on today's code, which promotes directly.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: promotion after template edge removal now passes graph rules, as deletion and `dep rm` already do (REQ-04).
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Deletion, dependency edits and template edges derive dependent readiness through one command helper.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One helper and three call-site families in four files, each a local substitution.

title: Field and lifecycle updates carry their readiness corrections
description:
Make a single-issue state change derive its dependents' readiness inside its own mutation plan, so rejecting, completing or reopening an issue updates its dependents in the same redo record instead of in later sessions or not at all.

## Background

- `update_issue` (`crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:458`) publishes through `publish_captured_field_update` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2595`, derivation `derive_field_update` `:1275`) and then, when the issue entered a terminal state, calls `check_auto_transitions` (`issue.rs:539-541`), which lists every issue and publishes one further session per promotable dependent (`issue.rs:860-876`).
- `update_issue_state` (`issue.rs:664`) and `reject_issue` without a reason use the lifecycle `State` plan (`publish_captured_state_transition`, `mod.rs:2696`; `publish_captured_lifecycle_mutation`, `mod.rs:2765`) and run no cascade; `reject_issue` with a reason uses the field update (`issue.rs:685-700`) and none either. A dependent of a rejected blocker stays `Backlog`, and `jit validate` does not flag it because only demotions are violations (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:505-530`).
- No path demotes `Ready` dependents when an issue leaves `Done` or `Rejected`; `jit validate` then reports that stored readiness disagrees with the dependency graph.
- The command helper maps pure readiness corrections over a base and a projected issue set to mutation intents (promotion through graph rules, direct demotion).
- `crates/jit/tests/fast_issue/readiness_coherence_tests.rs:226-271` holds a property test over dependency edits that checks only the `Ready`-but-blocked direction.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `derive_field_update` and the lifecycle `State`, `Claim` and `Release` plans add the helper's corrections for the `Affected` scope of their own change to the plan they publish; `update_issue` no longer calls `check_auto_transitions`.
- [hard] REQ-02: A harness test rejects a blocker (with and without a reason) and shows its only-blocked dependent `Ready` within the same session; it fails on today's code, where the dependent stays `Backlog`.
- [hard] REQ-03: A harness test moves a `Done` blocker back to `InProgress` and shows its `Ready` dependent demoted to `Backlog` within the same session; it fails on today's code.
- [hard] REQ-04: The readiness property test also generates state changes of blockers into and out of `Done` and `Rejected`, and asserts after each edit that no issue is `Ready` while blocked or `Backlog` while unblocked.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: rejection promotes dependents, and leaving a terminal state demotes `Ready` dependents (REQ-02, REQ-03). The automatic Done path, the bulk path and `jit validate --fix` still publish their own follow-up sessions until those move.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Single-issue field and lifecycle state changes include dependent readiness corrections in their own redo record.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Two plan builders gain one helper call, plus three focused tests.

title: Automatic Done carries its readiness corrections
description:
Make the automatic transition to `Done`, taken when an issue's last gate passes, promote its dependents inside the same mutation plan rather than through a later scan.

## Background

- `auto_transition_to_done` (`crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:844-857`) publishes the `AutoDone` lifecycle plan (`CapturedLifecycleMutation::AutoDone`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:866`; arm at `:3088-3098`) and then calls `check_auto_transitions` (`issue.rs:853`), which lists every issue and publishes one session per promotable dependent.
- Its callers are the manual gate pass (`pass_gate`, `crates/jit/src/commands/gate.rs:876`) and the postcheck runner (`run_postchecks`, `crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs:1579`); postchecks run their checkers outside the repository lock, so the automatic Done stays its own mutation after them.
- `auto_transition_to_done` publishes through `publish_captured_auto_transition` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2743`) and `publish_captured_lifecycle_mutation` (`mod.rs:2765`), which opens a preflight session and a publishing session on every attempt. Each dependent that `check_auto_transitions` promotes goes through the same lifecycle path, so it adds two session opens.
- Field and lifecycle `State` plans already add the shared helper's readiness corrections to their own plan.
- Command tests count session opens with `SessionOpenCounter` (`crates/jit/src/commands/test_helpers.rs`), measuring a baseline run first as `crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs:1545` does.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The `AutoDone` lifecycle plan adds the helper's corrections for the `Affected` scope of its transition, and `auto_transition_to_done` no longer calls `check_auto_transitions`.
- [hard] REQ-02: A harness test passes the last manual gate of a `Gated` issue whose dependent is otherwise unblocked, shows the issue `Done` and the dependent `Ready`, and counts the same number of session opens as the identical pass with no dependent (baseline counter); it fails on today's code, where the dependent's promotion adds two session opens.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged apart from the corrections landing in one record with the transition.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: The automatic Done plan includes dependent promotions in its own redo record instead of a follow-up pass.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One plan arm gains one helper call and one session-count test.

title: Validate fix derives readiness through the shared helper
description:
Make the readiness part of `jit validate --fix` use the shared readiness derivation over every projected issue, so the repair and the mutation paths decide readiness with one function.

## Background

- After the one-mutation `--fix` change, `--fix` derives all fixes from one validation capture and publishes them in one mutation; its readiness step applies `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` to the projected issue set until no correction remains, inside `crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs`. Before that change the step is `check_pending_transitions` (`validate.rs:2076-2130`), which publishes one session per correction through `auto_transition_to_ready` and `auto_transition_to_backlog` (`validate.rs:2117-2118`).
- The pure domain readiness derivation returns every correction for a base and projected set under the `All` scope in one pass (a correction never changes another issue's blockedness), and the command helper maps corrections to intents, promoting through graph rules.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The `--fix` readiness step obtains its corrections from the shared derivation with the `All` scope through the shared command helper; no loop repeating `derive_readiness_correction` until a fixpoint remains in `validate.rs`.
- [hard] REQ-02: A harness test declares a graph rule that refuses the transition to `Ready` for one issue, seeds that issue `Backlog` while unblocked, and runs `--fix`: the issue stays `Backlog`, a `transition_blocked` event names the rule, and the fix report states the refused repair. It fails before this change: the one-mutation `--fix` applies each correction from `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` directly, so the issue is promoted despite the rule.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: a readiness promotion made by `--fix` now passes graph rules; a refused one is reported, as for every other promotion (REQ-02).
- That `--fix` publishes all its repairs in one mutation is owned by the one-mutation `--fix` change this entry follows; this entry adds no second test of it.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: validate --fix computes readiness repairs with the shared derivation over the whole projected set.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One fix step swaps its loop for the shared helper.

title: Post-commit readiness publishers are gone
description:
Delete the post-commit readiness machinery, now that every state- or dependency-changing plan carries its own corrections.

## Background

- `check_auto_transitions` (`crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:860-876`) lists every issue and publishes one `AutoReady` session per promotable issue. Its remaining caller is `apply_bulk_update` (`crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs:294-295`, guarded by an `entered_terminal` flag accumulated at `:264,274`), after the batch; the bulk path's per-issue field updates already carry their own corrections. A unit test owns it (`test_check_auto_transitions_opens_sessions_only_for_eligible_backlog_issues`, `issue.rs:1040-1078`) and a `bulk_update.rs` comment cites that test (`:1527`).
- `auto_transition_to_ready` (`issue.rs:817`) has no other caller once `--fix` stopped publishing per correction; `auto_transition_to_backlog` (`issue.rs:834`) is gone or uncalled for the same reason.
- `publish_captured_auto_transition` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2743-2762`) maps `Ready`, `Backlog` and `Done` to the `AutoReady`, `AutoBacklog` and `AutoDone` lifecycle variants (`mod.rs:857-869`), whose arms sit at `mod.rs:3062-3087`; only `AutoDone` keeps a caller (`auto_transition_to_done`).
- The field-update outcome carries `entered_terminal` in two structs (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:1032,1042`; set at `:1484,1500,1542,2661,2675`). Its readers are `update_issue` (`issue.rs:539`, gone once single updates carry corrections) and the bulk flag above; after the bulk call goes, the fields are never read and fail clippy's dead-code check.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `check_auto_transitions`, `auto_transition_to_ready`, `auto_transition_to_backlog`, the `AutoReady` and `AutoBacklog` lifecycle variants with their arms, and both `entered_terminal` fields with their assignments no longer exist; the automatic transition entry point accepts only the `Done` target.
- [hard] REQ-02: No production code path publishes a session whose only purpose is a readiness correction after another mutation committed.
- [hard] REQ-03: A harness test bulk-updates a blocker to `Done` and shows its dependent `Ready` in the blocker's own publication, with no extra session (session counter); the deleted unit test is replaced by it.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged: the corrections these functions published are already in each primary plan.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: No command publishes a follow-up session to correct readiness after its primary mutation commits.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Deletion of one cascade family after its callers moved.

title: Missing-lease refusal is one typed error
description:
Define the missing-lease refusal once, as a typed error whose `Display` is the message, so strict mode returns it and warn mode renders it.

## Background

- The message `No active lease for issue {id}.\nAcquire lease with: jit claim acquire {id}` is formatted in `captured_lease_warnings` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:774-812`, text at `:801`) and in `require_active_lease` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:3395`, text at `:3409`). A third copy in the template lease warnings (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:277-316`, text at `:306`) goes away when template warnings come from `captured_lease_warnings`, which is the state this issue starts from.
- Strict mode returns the text through `anyhow!`/`bail!` (`mod.rs:807`, `:3412-3414`), so callers and `crates/jit/src/output/failure.rs` can match it only by string.
- Tests assert the text: `crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:2168` (`test_delete_issue_retries_when_lease_mode_changes_after_preflight`), `crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs:3817` (`test_strict_lease_rejection_precedes_external_precheck`), `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:4307`, and `crates/jit/tests/cli_gate/gate_cli_integration_test.rs:379,394`.
- Error types live in `crates/jit/src/errors.rs` as `thiserror` structs (for example `LeaseNotFoundError`, `:392`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `crates/jit/src/errors.rs` defines `LeaseRequiredError` naming the issue, and its `Display` is the only place the missing-lease message text is written.
- [hard] REQ-02: In strict mode both lease checks return an error that downcasts to `LeaseRequiredError`; in warn mode they push its rendered `Display` as the warning.
- [hard] REQ-03: A unit test asserts that a strict refusal downcasts to `LeaseRequiredError` (this fails today, when the refusal is an untyped `anyhow` message), and the existing message assertions pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged: the warning and error text stay byte-identical, and the process exit status is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: LeaseRequiredError defines the missing-lease message once for strict refusals and warn-mode warnings.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One error type replaces two inline message strings in one module.

title: Claims-first lease checks inside the publishing session
description:
Move the lease checks of issue assign, issue unassign and the gate attach, pass and fail commands into the session that publishes their change, keeping a strict refusal ahead of any checker, and delete the lock-free pre-session check.

## Background

- `require_active_lease` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:3395`) and `check_active_lease` (`:3335`) read lease state outside the claims lock and before the publishing session opens, with the mode taken from the executor's disk-backed configuration cache (`self.cached_config()`, `:3400`). They are called before publication by `assign_issue` (`crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:704`, check at `:712`), `unassign_issue` (`issue.rs:745`, `:753`), `add_gates` (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate.rs:696`, `:715`), `remove_gates` (`gate.rs:742`, `:761`), `pass_gate` (`gate.rs:786`, `:807`) and `fail_gate` (`gate.rs:952`, `:972`). Their unit tests are at `mod.rs:4230,4258,4280,4312`.
- `pass_gate` runs an automated gate's checker through `check_gate_with` (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs:830`) after the lease check, so today a strict unleased automated pass is refused before the checker runs. `check_gate_with` captures its inputs in one session and records the run in a second; the checker runs between them, outside the lock. Upstream, the gate-capture and verdict-reuse changes rewrite this function: the inputs capture holds only the evaluated issue's latest runs, and a reusable verdict is looked up from one verdict record (today `reusable_verdict`, `gate_check.rs:1013`). The preliminary lease check is added to the inputs session as those changes leave it, ahead of both the reuse lookup and the checker. `gate evaluate-all` reaches the same path through `pass_all_gates` (`gate.rs:890`), which calls `pass_gate` per required gate.
- The in-session form already exists: the field update takes `claims_mutation_guard` (`mod.rs:753`) before `open_mutation_session` and calls `captured_lease_warnings` (`mod.rs:774`) with the captured mode and issues (`publish_captured_field_update`, `mod.rs:2595`). The guard is `None` outside a git repository, so warn mode warns and strict mode refuses (`@/charter/D-4`).
- The lifecycle path keeps a preliminary captured check for the same reason: it refuses a strict unleased transition with a preliminary guard over the preflight image before running prechecks, and repeats the check under the held guard when publishing (`publish_captured_lifecycle_mutation`, `mod.rs:2836-2856`; owning test `test_strict_lease_rejection_precedes_external_precheck`, `gate_check.rs:3774`). That refusal is part of the publishing operation, not a pre-session check, and stays.
- The dedicated commands publish through `publish_captured_issue_mutation` (`mod.rs:2294`; `SetManualGateStatus` for manual pass and fail, `mod.rs:489`).
- Lock order: the claims guard must be taken before any repository session. `issue assign` and `issue unassign` (`IssueCommands::coordinates_claims_first`, `crates/jit/src/cli.rs:2919`) and `gate add`, `gate remove`, `gate evaluate`, `gate evaluate-all`, `gate evaluate-many` and `gate fail` (`GateCommands::coordinates_claims_first`, `cli.rs:2952`) are classified repository-first and need recovery dispatch (`GateCommands::requires_recovery_dispatch`, `cli.rs:2785-2804`), so `crates/jit/src/main.rs:1876-1905` opens a startup session for them, and a claims guard taken afterwards is refused by the guard-order check (`crates/jit/src/storage/guard_order.rs`). `CLAIM_FIRST_LEAF_COMMANDS` (`cli.rs:3240`) and `test_claim_first_classification_covers_exact_cli_callers` (`cli.rs:3335`) pin the classification.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `require_active_lease` and `check_active_lease` no longer exist; assign, unassign, gate attach and removal, manual pass, manual fail and automated pass check the target issue's lease through `captured_lease_warnings` inside the session that publishes their change, holding the claims guard taken before that session.
- [hard] REQ-02: A strict unleased automated pass is refused through a preliminary captured lease check in `check_gate_with`'s inputs session, before the checker runs; a harness test with a checker that records its invocation shows the refusal with `LeaseRequiredError` and no checker run.
- [hard] REQ-03: `issue assign`, `issue unassign`, `gate add`, `gate remove`, `gate evaluate`, `gate evaluate-all`, `gate evaluate-many` and `gate fail` are classified claims-first, and the classification inventory test lists them (this assertion fails today).
- [hard] REQ-04: A harness test shows strict mode refusing an unleased assign with `LeaseRequiredError` while leaving the stored issue unchanged, and warn mode returning the warning with the assignment applied.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: these commands now read the lease under the claims lock and the mode from the captured configuration; outside a git repository, warn mode warns and strict mode refuses instead of failing on worktree-path resolution. The lifecycle path's preliminary refusal before prechecks is unchanged.
- Postcheck-driven automated passes are system-derived and check no lease.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Assign, unassign and gate commands check leases inside their publishing session, and the pre-session check is gone.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Six call sites move one existing check into their sessions, with one classification change that must land with them for lock order.

title: Template application checks leases in its publishing session
description:
Check template application's lease targets inside the session that publishes the template's edits, and drop the separate preflight session that exists only to compute them.

## Background

- `apply_template_request` (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:152`) opens a first session (`:170-191`) only to derive the lease targets and mode, computes warnings between sessions (`template_lease_warnings`, `:193`, defined `:277`; upstream lock-free reader work routes this through the guarded check `captured_lease_warnings`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:774`), then opens a second session, re-derives, and retries if the targets or mode changed (`:200-219`). The claims guard is not held across publication.
- `DerivedTemplateApply::lease_targets` (`template.rs:320`) and `existing_template_lease_targets` (`:265`) already name the existing issues the apply edits.
- `jit apply` is classified repository-first (`Commands::coordinates_claims_first`, `crates/jit/src/cli.rs:2701`, the `Self::Apply` arm at `:2726`), so its startup session is retained and a claims guard taken inside it would be refused by the guard-order check; `gate preset apply` is already claims-first. `CLAIM_FIRST_LEAF_COMMANDS` (`cli.rs:3240`) and `test_claim_first_classification_covers_exact_cli_callers` (`cli.rs:3335`) pin the claims-first leaves.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Template application takes the claims guard before its one publishing session and checks the captured lease targets with `captured_lease_warnings` inside that session; no session exists only to compute lease targets.
- [hard] REQ-02: `jit apply` is classified claims-first and the classification inventory test lists it.
- [hard] REQ-03: A harness test counting session opens shows one session per successful template apply attempt (today two), and strict mode refuses an apply that edits an unleased existing issue without publishing anything.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: the lease is read under the claims lock in the publishing session, and `jit apply` locks claims before the repository; the warnings and refusals are otherwise unchanged.

title: One state derivation for update and lifecycle transitions
description:
Give the issue state field one derivation: `jit issue update --state` and the lifecycle transitions (`jit claim`, state changes and rejection) run the same prechecks and the same divert of `Done` to `Gated`.

## Background

- The lifecycle path runs precheck gates when a `Ready` issue moves to `InProgress` (`lifecycle_requires_prechecks`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:884-893`, used in the preflight of `publish_captured_lifecycle_mutation` `:2765`, at `:2794`, and rechecked at `:2911`; `captured_precheck_plan` `:655`). Checkers run in that preflight, outside the repository lock, and a strict unleased request is refused before they run (`:2836-2849`). The lifecycle path diverts `Done` with unpassed gates to `Gated` (`mod.rs:3101-3125`).
- The field path (`derive_field_update`, `mod.rs:1275`; published by `publish_captured_field_update` `:2595`), which `jit issue update --state` and bulk update use, has its own `Done`-to-`Gated` divert (`mod.rs:1383-1404`) and runs no precheck: with an automatic precheck gate whose checker fails, `jit issue update <id> --state in_progress` still moves the issue to `InProgress`.
- A unit test in `crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:3580-3590` calls `lifecycle_requires_prechecks` through `capture_mutation_preflight`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One state derivation decides a state change for both the field and the lifecycle paths: prechecks are a captured precondition of any `Ready` to `InProgress` change, run in the preflight as today, and one place diverts `Done` with unpassed gates to `Gated`.
- [hard] REQ-02: A test sets an automatic precheck gate whose checker fails on a `Ready` issue and shows `jit issue update --state in_progress` refused with the issue left `Ready`; it fails on today's code, which moves the issue.
- [hard] REQ-03: The existing lifecycle precheck, claim, lease-before-precheck and divert tests pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: `jit issue update --state in_progress` runs prechecks (in a preflight outside the repository lock, as `jit claim` does) and is refused when one fails.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

title: Bulk field changes write the single-update events
description:
